A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ξ-VI research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 Section 4 and its empirical appendices report original simulated linear-regression results and posterior-inference comparisons on Eight Schools.

after.justification: V3 Section 3 and its empirical appendix report original linear-regression simulations and Eight Schools inference results.

M1.justification: The Ξ-VI objective, Sinkhorn correction, and full coordinate-ascent procedure remain; v1 Algorithm 2 becomes v3 Algorithm 1. However, v3 removes the optional Gaussian pseudomarginal construction blending EP and MFVI precisions in v1 Appendix B, Eq. (B.7). V1 explicitly states that this variant was not implemented.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the bivariate Gaussian example, simulated Bayesian linear regression with a Laplace prior, and Eight Schools hierarchical inference. No new dataset, population, or distinct test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained comparisons use the same methods: EP and MFVI for regression, and MFVI, normalizing-flow VI, full-rank ADVI, and SVGD for Eight Schools. V3's prominent normalizing-flow comparison was already present in v1, including Appendix Figure 11.

E3.justification: V3 drops the evaluation of standard-deviation approximation error across 25 randomly sampled school pairs, removing that metric and sampling procedure. Retained evaluations preserve the stated data generation, coefficient grouping, support-point counts, MCMC budgets, posterior sample counts, regularization sweeps, and Sinkhorn tolerance. Changed plots do not establish changes to those settings.

E4.justification: V3 removes the pairwise treatment-difference standard-deviation error analyses in v1 Figures 5 and 10 and the MCMC-versus-MFVI correlation heatmaps in Figure 9. These supplied complementary checks of dependence recovery. Regularization sensitivity, joint-distribution contours, and the ten-pair credible-interval table remain.

E5.justification: The posterior credible-interval reporting and stated MCMC chain/convergence diagnostics remain. Neither version reports independent experimental repetition counts, seeds, confidence intervals for performance estimates, or significance tests. Revised posterior intervals are result changes, not a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Eight Schools results are substantially revised: Figure 4 changes reported credible intervals, and v3 Figure 5 changes Ξ-VI error curves and comparator levels relative to v1 Figure 11. Normalizing flow now matches Ξ-VI around λ=1 in W2 and λ=D in KL, replacing the earlier broad superiority finding. Pairwise-error and correlation results disappear, while every numerical entry in Appendix Table 1 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: The central linear-model result changes from v1 Theorem 4 to v3 Theorem 3. Bayes-optimality thresholds previously using ||B−B'_diag||² tr(Cov(theta)) are replaced by conditions involving tr(Cov(B_off theta)) and curvature constants; the overlap condition changes accordingly. The supporting expressivity bound and proof are rewritten in v3 Lemma 9. Most other asymptotic and stability results are retained through relocation.

C1.justification: The introduction shifts from claiming that Ξ-VI outperforms MFVI and other VI methods to emphasizing competitive performance against ADVI, normalizing flow, and SVGD. The principal contributions—expressivity regularization, EOT computation, frequentist guarantees, and conditional polynomial-time tractability—remain.

C2.justification: V3 explains why diagonal regression designs permit any λ in the Bayes-optimal regime and qualifies the empirical comparison with normalizing flow. It also changes the prose following the Bernstein–von Mises theorem: unlike v1's regularized finite-positive-λ limit, v3 describes the exact Gaussian limit, contradicting the retained theorem's third case.

D1.justification: V3 adds explicit Monte Carlo potential-update formulas in Section 2.2, documenting the existing sampled computation. It removes v1 Appendix B's EP/BBVI pseudocode and stopping/learning-rate guidance, and shortens the Eight Schools implementation account, including the explicit M^10-to-8M^3 storage reduction. No code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: V3 adds connections to generalized Bayes and PAC-Bayes, with references including Knoblauch et al., Alquier, and Wild et al., and supplies citations for existing ADVI, normalizing-flow, and SVGD comparisons. It removes the blanket characterization that competing extensions generally lack theory. The main VI/EOT positioning remains; Lacker et al.'s publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the introduction and methodological narrative, foregrounds expressivity-corrected mean-field VI, and places examples before asymptotic theory. Full coordinate ascent, computational complexity, and finite-sample stability move to appendices, while proofs are reorganized into separate appendices. This substantially changes the reading structure.

P2.justification: V3 redraws major figures with revised typography, legends, axes, and method ordering. Eight Schools accuracy and runtime displays from v1 Figures 6, 7, and 11 are consolidated into Figure 5. Other diagnostic figures disappear, the regression covariance figure is retained as Figure 6, and Table 1 is relocated. Headers and document layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: V3 improves navigation, explains the practical computation more explicitly, and more fairly acknowledges normalizing-flow competitiveness. These gains coexist with removed diagnostic evidence and implementation guidance. Moreover, its revised theoretical support contains a factor-of-four inconsistency in Lemma 9's displayed gradient equality and a misleading finite-positive-λ interpretation after Theorem 1. The clearer presentation and revised claims therefore do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
